content.text: {"id":"7c24a551-c84f-4024-9877-e42a82d37cac","audio_id":"ba22e0fa-2cf7-4297-aa44-44f2dbfd92f2","status":"complete","created_at":"2026-11-16T07:14:40Z","answer":"The lead is a bright, clearly articulated Korean vocal with a playful, child-directed delivery. In the main chorus, 고양이 and 강아지 are sung distinctly rather than rushed or malformed; their syllables sit within longer, connected melodic phrases, with a lilting, stepwise/arching contour and a resolving phrase ending. The backing gives those phrases a buoyant two-beat, oom-pah-like bounce. The verse is more stop-start and call-and-response, with short question/answer-like vocal bits over held accompaniment; the chorus opens into a more continuous tune. The ending is not audibly clipped, and there are brief fills rather than a long instrumental gap. So this recording itself has longer connected melodic phrases and a two-beat feel; I’m not making claims about having heard the comparison track."}
